about.title: Sebastopol Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Sebastopol is a small city, but its two-lane corridors — Rt 116, Bodega Avenue, Rt 12, and Petaluma Avenue — carry a steady flow of local and pass-through traffic. Public records show 8 injury collisions and 9 people injured in the most recent final year, with reports clustering on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., a window when school pickups, farm traffic, and commuters heading toward Highway 116 all overlap. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: insurers move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memory fades quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly. We simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney in the area who can look at what happened, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid common mistakes with insurance adjusters while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Runs Fast
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but claims against a government entity — say, over a road defect on Bodega Avenue — can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can flag which deadline applies before it quietly passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces your payout under pure comparative fault. Insurers know this and often try to pin extra fault on you early — before you've even seen the police report.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Pain Matters, But Proving It Does Too
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so there's no artificial ceiling on what a serious injury might be worth. That said, those damages still have to be documented and argued, which is exactly what a contingency-fee attorney is positioned to help with — no fee unless you recover.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to shift blame or minimize your injuries, even if they sound friendly. An independent attorney can help you understand what you're required to share versus what can wait.

items.question: Why do so many Sebastopol crashes get reported on Thursday afternoons?
items.answer: Public crash records show Thursday between 3 and 5 p.m. as a common reporting window locally, which lines up with school dismissal, farm and delivery traffic, and commuters converging near corridors like Rt 116 and Petaluma Avenue. This is a pattern in the data, not a judgment about any particular road or driver. If your crash happened during this window, it can still help to gather any nearby business camera footage quickly, since it may not be retained long.

items.question: What if my crash involved a city vehicle or happened on a poorly maintained road?
items.answer: Claims involving a government entity, such as the City of Sebastopol or Sonoma County, often come with a much shorter notice deadline than the standard two-year statute of limitations — sometimes as short as six months. Missing that window can end a claim before it starts, so it's worth having someone review the details promptly.
